Chapter Six Hundred Eighty-Nine

Romans 11:1 — Scar Tissue of the Soul and the 'Big Blot Out'; Preparation for Romans 11

Romans 11:1 “I ask, then, has God rejected his people? By no means! For I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, a member of the tribe of Benjamin.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: I say then, has God pushed away His people? Absolutely not! For I also am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

Romans 11 opens with one of the most consequential questions in the entire epistle: has God permanently set aside the nation of Israel? Before that question can be answered — before any verse of this chapter can be rightly understood — a foundational doctrine must be firmly established. That doctrine is scar tissue of the soul, and the phenomenon the apostle Paul describes as the national 'big blot out.' Every line of Romans 11, from verse 1 through verse 36, depends on a clear grasp of this principle. The present chapter lays that groundwork, drawing on the Old Testament record of Israel's repeated rejection of divine revelation and on the Christological titles embedded in the Shema of Deuteronomy 6:4. It also sets the stage for an examination of Revelation 1:7–8, which John writes as the New Testament completion of that ancient confession.

I. Scar Tissue of the Soul and the 'Big Blot Out'

The record holder for scar tissue of the soul prior to Israel's national blot out is Pharaoh — Amenhotep II, the great pharaoh of the Exodus. The pattern established in his case applies to every subsequent generation of Israel and, by extension, to every individual who persistently refuses divine truth.

A. The Mechanics of Soul Hardening

When a person hears truth and says no, the soul begins to accumulate what Scripture depicts as hardness in the right lobe — the faculty of spiritual perception and volitional response. Each successive refusal compounds the damage. The mind loses its capacity to think accurately, to reason from sound premises, or to distinguish reality from falsehood.

The Greek term pōrōsis (πώρωσις), rendered 'hardening' or 'blindness' in most translations, describes precisely this condition. It refers to the callousing of the cardiac faculty — the right lobe of the soul — through sustained negative volition toward truth. The result is what the present chapter terms 'scar tissue of the soul': an accumulated barrier that progressively prevents accurate perception of divine reality.

Once this vacuum opens in the soul, false content rushes in to fill it — a process Paul will describe more fully in Romans 1:21–28. The premises adopted by a soul in this condition are invariably false. Every logical chain built on a false premise, whether the reasoning is valid or invalid, arrives at a false conclusion. This accounts for the otherwise inexplicable spectacle of intelligent people arriving at catastrophically wrong judgments about the most fundamental questions of life.

B. Israel as the Paradigm Case

Israel provides the most fully documented case of this phenomenon in all of Scripture, which is one of the reasons the Old Testament record exists for the benefit of the Church Age believer. From the Exodus to the Virgin Birth — approximately fifteen hundred years — the pattern repeated itself in every generation. A majority would say no to divine revelation at the point of God-consciousness, no to the gospel, and no to the specific doctrine of the Hypostatic Union as embedded in the Mosaic revelation.

Yet in each of those generations, the Lord Jesus Christ personally appeared to individuals under scar tissue of the soul and reverse-process reversionism, making one final appeal under conditions specifically designed to arrest attention. He appeared as the Angel of Jehovah, or sent a supernatural messenger, working miracles that were objectively undeniable. The response was still refusal. People who witnessed genuine miracles performed by the second person of the Trinity said no. This establishes that they were entirely without excuse — not victims of insufficient evidence, but deliberate refusers of overwhelming evidence.

This is the background without which Romans 11:1 is unanswerable. The question 'Has God pushed away His people?' cannot be addressed until the reader understands the accumulation of rejection that preceded the national blot out, and the sustained grace that God extended before that point was reached. Romans 9 established Pharaoh as the record holder; Romans 11 draws the national conclusion.

C. The Sustaining Pivot

In every generation, however, a remnant of mature believers existed whose positive volition sustained divine blessing on the nation. This is what the commentary tradition on Romans calls the 'pivot' — the body of believers within a national entity whose adjustment to the justice of God creates a basis for logistical grace to continue flowing to the nation as a whole. The same principle holds for any national entity in the Church Age. Romans 11 will develop this explicitly. The present chapter simply establishes the framework: negative volition in the majority does not eliminate divine faithfulness toward the minority, and through that minority toward the whole.

II. The Shema and the Christological Titles of the God of Israel

Before Romans 11 can be exegeted verse by verse, a second foundational element must be clear: the specific Christological content of Deuteronomy 6:4, the Shema. This is not a peripheral point; it is the doctrinal axis around which Israel's entire history of acceptance and rejection rotates.

A. Deuteronomy 6:4 — The Two-Part Confession

The Hebrew of Deuteronomy 6:4 reads: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהוָה אֶחָד — transliterated: Shema Yisra'el, Adonai Eloheinu, Adonai Echad. The confession divides into two distinct theological affirmations.

The first affirmation is: the LORD is our God. The divine name rendered 'LORD' in most English translations is the covenant name of God, pointing to the self-existent, eternal deity. The possessive 'our God' — Eloheinu — establishes the covenant relationship between the Lord Jesus Christ as the second person of the Trinity and the nation of Israel. The Father is not the God of Israel in this technical covenantal sense. The Holy Spirit is not the God of Israel in this sense. The second person of the Trinity is the God of Israel, and this is testified throughout the Old Testament theophanies, the Angel of Jehovah appearances, and the prophetic literature.

The second affirmation turns on the Hebrew word echad (אֶחָד). This term is standardly translated 'one,' giving rise to the monotheistic formula: the LORD is one. That translation is correct, but it is incomplete. In biblical Hebrew, echad carries the additional semantic weight of uniqueness — oneness in the sense of being in a class by itself, incomparable, singular. This semantic range was recognized within the Jewish tradition, though it was not always applied to the specific Christological content embedded in the confession.

B. The Hypostatic Union as the Completion of the Shema

The full theological content of Deuteronomy 6:4 — particularly the uniqueness conveyed by echad — points forward to what Isaiah developed in chapters 7 through 9: the doctrine of Emmanuel, God with us. The God of Israel, who is eternal God and therefore has always existed, would become man. Not a theophanic appearance in human form, as at the tent of Abraham or at the wrestling match with Jacob, but actual, genuine humanity — a member of the human race by means of the Virgin Birth.

This is the uniqueness that echad encodes. The God of Israel is unique precisely because he is both eternal God and true man — two natures in one person. He is different from the Father and the Spirit in that he has assumed humanity. He is different from all other human beings in that he is simultaneously God. This is the Hypostatic Union, and this is what the Shema, rightly understood, was already teaching Israel from the days of Moses.

The stumbling block of Israel — the specific content of Israel's rejection that precipitated the blot out — is precisely the first advent: the incarnation of the God of Israel in true humanity, born of a virgin, presented as the Messiah. This rejection did not begin with the generation of Christ's ministry. It was the culmination of fifteen hundred years of accumulated refusal, generation by generation, to accept both affirmations of the Shema: (1) Adonai Eloheinu — Jesus Christ is eternal God; (2) Adonai Echad — Jesus Christ is uniquely the God-man, Hypostatic Union, Virgin Birth.

III. Revelation 1:7–8 — John's Completion of Deuteronomy 6:4

John, the last surviving apostle, writing in AD 96 on the island of Patmos, brings the doctrinal trajectory of the Shema to its New Testament completion in Revelation 1:7–8. The passage concerns the second advent of the Lord Jesus Christ and must be read against the Old Testament background established above.

A. Revelation 1:7 — Exegetical Analysis

Revelation 1:7 “Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him, and all tribes of the earth will wail on account of him. Even so. Amen.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: Now listen carefully — He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, including those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over Him. Yes, amen.

The opening particle is idou (ἰδού), the aorist middle imperative of horaō (ὁράω), functioning as a demonstrative particle of concentration and perception. It is equivalent to the English transition 'now listen carefully' — a directive to focus on what follows as something of supreme importance.

The main verb is the present middle indicative of erchomai (ἔρχομαι), correctly rendered 'he is coming.' This is a futuristic present: the second advent had not yet occurred when John wrote in 96 AD, but it is stated in the present tense because it is so certain in the divine program that it may be conceived as already in process. This use of the present tense corresponds to the Hebrew prophetic perfect — the idiom by which prophets described future events as accomplished because of the absolute certainty of divine fulfillment.

The middle voice is indirect middle, stressing the Lord Jesus Christ as the agent who produces the action of returning. The prepositional phrase that follows is meta (μετά) plus the genitive plural of nephelē (νεφέλη), 'with clouds.' Clouds in this eschatological context are not meteorological phenomena but a standard biblical symbol for vast multitudes — armies or innumerable people. The Old Testament precedents include Isaiah 60:8, Jeremiah 4:13, and the New Testament precedent of Hebrews 12:1. The clouds that accompany Christ at the second advent are the resurrected and raptured members of the royal family of God, returning with him — every Church Age believer who has died or been raptured, now in resurrection bodies.

B. 'Every Eye Will See Him' — The Supernatural Darkness

The phrase 'every eye will see him' employs the predictive future of horaō (ὁράω), dynamic middle voice, with the direct object auton (αὐτόν) referring to the Lord Jesus Christ. The statement raises an immediate geographical question: since the earth is a sphere rotating on its axis, one hemisphere is always in darkness and the other in light. How can every eye on both hemispheres simultaneously see the returning Christ?

The answer lies in the supernatural darkness that Scripture extensively predicts as accompanying the second advent. The entire earth will be enshrouded in a complete, impenetrable supernatural darkness — a darkness that no artificial light can penetrate. Search lights, artillery flares, and electrical illumination will be useless. This total envelopment eliminates the day-night distinction imposed by the earth's rotation relative to the sun. Against that universal darkness, the Lord Jesus Christ — who is the light of the world — will be visible from every point on the globe simultaneously. His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives at Jerusalem, but the light of his appearing will penetrate to every side of the spherical earth.

The eschatological passages describing this supernatural darkness include: Isaiah 13:9–10; Ezekiel 32:7–8; Joel 2:10–11; Joel 3:15; Amos 5:18; Zechariah 14:6; Matthew 24:29; Luke 21:25–27; and Revelation 6:12. A precursor of this same darkness occurred locally at the cross, during the period when the personal sins of the entire human race were being imputed to Christ and judged. The Father enshrouded the cross in darkness during that agonizing interval, granting the Son privacy in bearing the judgment that accomplished salvation. That local darkness prefigures the universal darkness of the second advent.

The Armageddon Campaign is in progress at the time of Christ's return. The armies of the king of the north, assembled to crack into Jerusalem, will be halted by this impenetrable darkness. It is within this context that 'every eye will see him' — including those who pierced him, a reference to the generation of Israelites responsible for the crucifixion, raised for this moment of recognition. The exegesis of that phrase, and the meaning of the mourning of all the tribes of the earth, will be taken up in the continuation of this study.

Conclusions from Chapter Six Hundred Eighty-Nine

1. Scar tissue of the soul is the governing category for understanding Romans 11. Every verse of the chapter — from the question of Israel's rejection in verse 1 through the doxology of verse 36 — presupposes the reader's grasp of this principle. Accumulated negative volition toward divine truth produces a progressive hardening of the right lobe that renders accurate perception impossible, even in the presence of miraculous evidence.

2. The mechanics of soul hardening follow a fixed sequence. Truth is presented; the will refuses; capacity for truth perception diminishes; false content fills the resulting vacuum; the premises adopted become systematically false; every conclusion drawn from those premises, however logically constructed, is therefore false. This is not a temporary condition but a progressive and ultimately catastrophic one.

3. Israel provides the definitive historical paradigm of this phenomenon. Over approximately fifteen hundred years, from the Exodus to the first advent, the Lord Jesus Christ made repeated supernatural appeals to Israelites under scar tissue of the soul — appearing as the Angel of Jehovah, working undeniable miracles, sending prophets with specific doctrinal content. The consistent response of the majority in each generation was refusal. They are therefore entirely without excuse.

4. The pivot sustained Israel across every generation of the blot out. In each period of national apostasy, a remnant of mature believers — positive toward doctrine and adjusted to the justice of God — provided the basis for continued logistical grace to the nation. The existence of this pivot does not eliminate divine discipline on the negative majority, but it delays and limits the cycles of national discipline. Romans 11 will develop this explicitly.

5. The Shema of Deuteronomy 6:4 encodes two Christological affirmations. The first — Adonai Eloheinu, 'the LORD is our God' — establishes the Lord Jesus Christ as the second person of the Trinity and the specific God of Israel by covenant. The second — Adonai Echad, 'the LORD is unique' — points forward to the Hypostatic Union: the God of Israel would become man by means of the Virgin Birth, uniting full deity and genuine humanity in one person. Israel's rejection of the first advent is the rejection of the second affirmation of their own foundational confession.

6. John's Revelation 1:7 completes the doctrinal trajectory of the Shema. Writing in AD 96, the apostle John brings the Old Testament confession of Deuteronomy 6:4 to its New Testament completion by describing the second advent: the God of Israel, uniquely God and man, returns visibly to the earth in the same humanity he assumed at the first advent. The futuristic present tense of erchomai — 'he is coming' — expresses absolute certainty of a future event, corresponding to the Hebrew prophetic perfect.

7. The 'clouds' accompanying Christ at the second advent are the royal family of God. Following the standard biblical use of clouds as a symbol for vast multitudes (Isaiah 60:8; Jeremiah 4:13; Hebrews 12:1), the clouds of Revelation 1:7 represent the resurrected and raptured Church Age believers who return with the Lord Jesus Christ in resurrection bodies. Every living Church Age believer who has died or been raptured will be part of this returning company.

8. Universal visibility at the second advent is achieved through supernatural darkness. The earth will be completely enshrouded in impenetrable supernatural darkness at the moment of Christ's return, eliminating the day-night distinction produced by the earth's rotation. No artificial light will function. Against this total darkness, the returning Christ — the light of the world — will be visible from every point on the globe simultaneously. This darkness is attested in Isaiah 13:9–10; Ezekiel 32:7–8; Joel 2:10–11; Joel 3:15; Amos 5:18; Zechariah 14:6; Matthew 24:29; Luke 21:25–27; and Revelation 6:12. Its precursor was the local darkness at the cross.

9. The exegesis of Revelation 1:7b — 'those who pierced him' — awaits completion. The identification of those who pierced him, and the precise character of the mourning of all the tribes of the earth, will be examined in the continuation of this study as the passage connects directly with the question of Israel's restoration in Romans 11.

Glossary

Glossary

Term Greek / Transliteration Definition
pōrōsis πώρωσις pōrōsis — hardening, callousness Noun from pōroō, to harden or callous. Describes the progressive hardening of the right lobe of the soul through sustained negative volition toward divine truth. Rendered 'hardening' or 'blindness' in most English translations of Romans 11:25 and Ephesians 4:18.
echad אֶחָד echad — one; unique Hebrew numeral and adjective bearing the dual semantic range of numerical oneness and uniqueness. In Deuteronomy 6:4 it affirms both the monotheistic unity of God and the incomparable uniqueness of the God of Israel — a uniqueness fulfilled in the Hypostatic Union of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Eloheinu אֱלֹהֵינוּ Eloheinu — our God First person plural possessive form of Elohim. In Deuteronomy 6:4 it designates the Lord Jesus Christ as the God of Israel by covenant relationship — the second person of the Trinity as the specific divine patron of the nation.
Shema שְׁמַע Shema — hear, listen attentively Qal imperative of shama', to hear or heed. The opening word of Deuteronomy 6:4, giving its name to the central confession of Judaism. Carries the force of directed, obedient attention — not mere auditory reception but volitional response to what is heard.
idou ἰδού idou — behold; now listen carefully Aorist middle imperative of horaō functioning as a demonstrative particle of concentration. Used in Revelation 1:7 to arrest the reader's attention before a statement of supreme doctrinal importance. Equivalent in force to the English 'now listen carefully.'
erchomai ἔρχομαι erchomai — to come, to go Standard Greek verb of motion. In Revelation 1:7 it is used in the futuristic present tense — the second advent stated as already in process because of its absolute certainty in the divine program. Corresponds to the Hebrew prophetic perfect.
nephelē νεφέλη nephelē — cloud Standard Greek noun for cloud. In eschatological contexts (Revelation 1:7; Matthew 24:30; 1 Thessalonians 4:17) it functions as a symbol for vast multitudes — armies or innumerable people — following the established biblical idiom of Isaiah 60:8, Jeremiah 4:13, and Hebrews 12:1.
horaō ὁράω horaō — to see, to perceive Greek verb of visual and mental perception. In Revelation 1:7 the predictive future indicative, dynamic middle voice, conveys that every human being alive at the second advent will personally witness the return of Christ — made possible by the supernatural darkness that enshrouds the earth at that moment.
Hypostatic Union The theological term for the union of full, undiminished deity and genuine humanity in the one person of the Lord Jesus Christ. The two natures are united without mixture, confusion, or alteration. In the present chapter this doctrine is identified as the specific Christological content that Israel was required to accept under Deuteronomy 6:4 and that constituted the primary stumbling block precipitating the national blot out.
pivot The body of mature believers within a national entity whose consistent adjustment to the justice of God provides the basis for continued logistical grace to the nation. In every generation of Israel, a pivot of positive believers sustained divine blessing despite the majority's negative volition. The same principle operates in any nation during the Church Age.
scar tissue of the soul Accumulated hardness in the right lobe of the soul resulting from sustained negative volition toward divine truth. Progressive in its development, it eventually renders the soul incapable of accurate perception of reality and opens it to false content through the vacuum created by the absence of truth. See also: pōrōsis; blackout of the soul; vacuum of the soul.
futuristic present A Greek grammatical idiom in which a future event is stated in the present tense to express absolute certainty of its fulfillment. The event is conceived as already in process in the mind of the speaker or writer. Equivalent to the Hebrew prophetic perfect. Exemplified by erchomai in Revelation 1:7.

Chapter Six Hundred Ninety

Revelation 1:7–8 · Introduction to Romans 11 · The Big Blot Out · Alpha and Omega

Revelation 1:7 “Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him, and all tribes of the earth will wail on account of him. Even so. Amen.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: Behold, he is coming with clouds, and every eye will see him — also those who pierced him — and all the tribes with reference to the land shall lament over him. Yes, I believe it.
Revelation 1:8 “"I am the Alpha and the Omega," says the Lord God, "who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty."” (ESV)
Corrected translation: I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord — the one who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.

This chapter completes the exegesis of Revelation 1:7–8, which serves as the extended introduction to Romans 11. The passage establishes the eschatological setting of the second advent, identifies two categories of Jews who will be present on the earth at that moment, and introduces the theological subject that will dominate Romans 11: Israel — her heritage, her failure, her future, and what her history reveals about the individual believer's soul.

I. Revelation 1:7 — Those Who Pierced Him: The Big Blot Out at the Second Advent

The Qualitative Relative Pronoun: hostis

The phrase and they also which pierced him is governed by the qualitative relative pronoun hostis (ὅστις). The qualitative relative pronoun does not simply identify persons but designates persons who belong to a particular category. Here that category is Jewish unbelievers — those who, in every generation from the Exodus to the cross, exercised maximum negative volition toward the first advent of Christ. This phenomenon is designated the big blot out: the systematic, sustained rejection of Christ as Savior that blots the first advent entirely out of Jewish consciousness.

The verb pierced is the aorist active indicative of the Greek verb ekkenteo. The aorist tense is constative, gathering into one entirety every Jew in history who has been guilty of the big blot out. The active voice indicates that these Jews — those who rejected Christ as Savior — produced the action: they built up scar tissue of the soul and hardened their hearts through sustained negative volition that culminated at the first advent. The indicative mood declares the historical reality of this phenomenon in every generation from Moses to the second advent.

Corrected translation: also those who pierced him — those who blotted out the first advent.

All the Tribes with Reference to the Land: phyle and ge

The phrase rendered all kindreds of the earth in the Authorized Version requires correction. All is the nominative plural of the adjective pas (πᾶς), correctly translated all. The noun phyle (φυλή) means tribes — specifically the tribes of Israel. The accompanying noun is the genitive singular of reference of ge (γῆ), which in this context refers not to the earth in general but to the land — the holy land, the land of Israel. The corrected translation is therefore: and all the tribes with reference to the land.

The verb translated wail is the future middle indicative of kopto, meaning to strike the breast, to wail, to lament — the physical expression of mourning in the ancient world. The gesture involved striking the chest and crying out in anguish, a public demonstration that something of supreme value had been irretrievably lost. In context, kopto expresses the frustration of Jewish unbelievers who, at the moment of the second advent, recognize what they have rejected. They were saturated with both natural and supernatural evangelism throughout the tribulation — by the 144,000, by Moses and Elijah, by angelic proclamation — and said no at every point. When every eye sees him, their moment of final, irreversible recognition has arrived.

Corrected translation of Revelation 1:7: Behold, he is coming with clouds, and every eye will see him — also those who pierced him — and all the tribes with reference to the land shall lament over him. Yes, I believe it.

The Lamenting as Frustration, Not Repentance

The lamentation of kopto is frustration, not saving repentance. These are Jewish unbelievers who, during the most concentrated period of evangelism in all of history, repeatedly heard the gospel in supernatural clarity and repeatedly refused it. Their exposure to the gospel was unparalleled: 144,000 Jewish evangelists, two witnesses with miraculous authentication, angelic messengers. They were evangelized in terms that required no interpretation, no cultural translation, no ambiguity. They understood. Understanding, they refused. Sustained negative volition built scar tissue of the soul until they no longer recognized what they were refusing — until the moment Christ himself appeared.

The frustration of that moment parallels, in an ultimate eschatological key, what every human being encounters when proximity to truth is greatest and the volition has been systematically closed against it. To be so close — in heritage, in instruction, in supernatural confirmation — and yet to have missed it entirely: this is the content of kopto. They follow the pattern of Esau, who sold his birthright for a bowl of lentils. The birthright of Israel is incomparable: the covenants, the scriptures, the prophets, the first advent, the Messiah himself. The selling price was the accumulated negative volitions of generations. The loss is total and eternal.

They will be removed from the earth by the baptism of fire before the millennium begins. Their frustration in that moment represents the terminal expression of the same frustration experienced by every Jewish unbeliever in history who possessed the heritage of Israel and refused it.

II. The Principle: Living in the Light of Eternity

The lamentation of Jewish unbelievers at the second advent raises a universal principle that applies to every believer in the Church Age. For most believers, the point of final reckoning will not be the second advent but the moment of physical death — and in those final moments, everything in life that previously seemed compelling will lose its weight.

Wealth, achievement, social standing, the approval of others — none of these can be carried beyond physical death. What can be carried is the content of the soul: the Bible doctrine that has been metabolized through the grace apparatus for perception and stored in the right lobe as epignosis. That doctrine is permanent. Everything else is left behind.

The believer dying the sin unto death faces a moment analogous, in kind if not in degree, to the frustration of kopto: the recognition that what was offered freely every day — doctrine, momentum, the protocol plan of God — was neglected in favor of what cannot survive the grave. There is no condemnation, no loss of salvation; heaven is certain. But the absence of reward, the forfeited supergrace blessing, the wasted years — these become vivid at the point of departure.

By contrast, the believer who has sustained daily doctrine intake, cracked the maturity barrier, and advanced to supergrace knows at the moment of death the reality of dying grace. The content of the soul — the accumulated treasure of epignosis — does accompany the departing believer. The judgment seat of Christ holds no terror for the mature believer; it is the formal ratification of what was established in time.

The principle: every day lived as unto the Lord, with sustained Bible doctrine intake and momentum in the protocol plan, is a day that cannot be taken away. The logistical grace of God — providing everything necessary for physical existence — makes this advance possible for every believer regardless of circumstance. The heritage of the royal family of God exceeds even the heritage of Israel, because it is eternal and unconditional. To possess such a heritage and neglect it is the maximum form of what kopto expresses at the second advent.

III. Israel as the Subject of Romans 11: A Photograph of the Individual Soul

The frustration of Revelation 1:7 introduces what will be the dominant subject of Romans 11: the Jew and Israel. This chapter of Romans represents the most concentrated theological and historical analysis of Israel in the New Testament canon. It is, however, more than a study of Jewish history. Israel's history with God functions as a photograph — a precise analogue — of the individual believer's soul. The patterns of Jewish positive and negative volition, of spiritual heritage received and rejected, of divine discipline and divine blessing, are the same patterns that govern the spiritual life of every Church Age believer.

The heritage of Israel is unparalleled in human history. The canon of Scripture was entrusted to Jews. The Lord Jesus Christ entered human history through the Jewish genetic line. The covenants — Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, New — were made with Israel. The apostolic authors of the New Testament, with one possible exception, were Jews. The Apostle Paul, the greatest theological intellect in human history, was a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin.

The tribe of Benjamin is significant. The great men of genius in Israel's history came predominantly from the tribe of Levi — Moses, the Levitical priests, the majority of the writing prophets. The tribe of Benjamin was the great warrior tribe. To find aggressive genius in the warrior tribe is rare: it combines intellectual power with the capacity for sustained, disciplined combat. Paul exemplifies this combination. He never served in the Roman military, yet his epistles are saturated with military analogies that arise not from observation alone but from the native disposition of an aggressive mind. His genius was not recessive — turned inward to a narrow field — but aggressive, applied to the full scope of divine revelation and communicated with a precision that has never been equaled.

The blessings that flow to Gentile civilization through Israel are not incidental. They are the consistent pattern of history. The principle of Zechariah's prophecy — ten Gentiles seizing the robe of one Jew and asking to accompany him to Jerusalem — will find its literal fulfillment in the millennium, but it describes a reality that has characterized all of human history: the blessing of the Lord flows to the nations through Israel. Romans 11 will document this with a precision that is without parallel in theological literature.

IV. Revelation 1:8 — I Am the Alpha and the Omega

Grammar and Identification

Verse 8 contains a formal self-identification by the Lord Jesus Christ. The nominative singular subject is the first person singular personal pronoun ego, referring to Christ. The verb is the present active indicative of eimi — I am. The static present represents a condition that exists perpetually; it is not a process or development but a permanent state of being. Since the first advent and the hypostatic union, the truth of this statement is taken for granted as a categorical fact. The active voice indicates that Jesus Christ produces the action of the verb — he is the one who declares and sustains this identity. The indicative mood is the mood of dogmatic assertion.

With this we have a predicate nominative — neuter singular, governed by the generic definite article to (τό). The generic article places Christ in a unique category: the God-man, the hypostatic union, set off in distinction from all other divine or human categories. He is not merely God; he is not merely man. He is the one person who is both simultaneously, without confusion and without diminution of either nature.

Alpha: The Eternal Deity of Christ

Alpha (ἄλφα) is the first letter of the Greek alphabet. The Greek alphabet was derived from the Phoenician, with the single modification that the Semitic cheth was adapted to become the Greek alpha. Alpha means the beginning. As Alpha, the Lord Jesus Christ is eternal God — the second person of the Trinity, co-equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Holy Spirit. The Alpha glory of Christ is related to his divine essence and his divine integrity. As Alpha, Christ was the creator of the universe and the God of Israel. The Alpha glory antedates creation; it is the glory Christ possessed with the Father before the world was (John 17:5).

Omega: The Glory of the Hypostatic Union

Omega (ὦ) is the last letter of the Greek alphabet. As Omega, Christ is in hypostatic union forever. The Omega glory of Christ begins with the first advent — the virgin birth — and encompasses the full scope of his incarnate work: impeccability, the saving work on the cross (redemption, reconciliation, propitiation), resurrection, ascension, and session at the right hand of the Father. The Omega glory will be permanently manifest to mankind at the second advent and throughout the millennium. Brief manifestations occurred during the first advent — the transfiguration, the post-resurrection appearances — but the full, perpetual display of the Omega glory awaits the second advent.

The Big Blot Out as Jewish Rejection of the Alpha-Omega Identity

The Jewish race was founded on recognition of the first advent. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were regenerate through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, whom they recognized as both God and Savior. The Mosaic Law — specifically its second code, the shadow code of the tabernacle and sacrificial system — was structured to present the first advent in comprehensive detail. The writing prophets amplified this presentation. The Jewish heritage, taken as a whole, was the most comprehensive first-advent presentation in history.

The big blot out is defined as maximum negative volition toward the first advent of Christ — specifically, the blotting out from Jewish consciousness of Christ as Adonai Elohenu Adonai Echad (the Lord our God, the Lord is one) and as the Savior-Messiah of Israel. Jewish unbelievers will accept almost any characterization of Jesus of Nazareth — teacher, prophet, moral reformer, religious leader, wise man — but the identification of Jesus as Adonai, as the God of Israel and the Savior of mankind, produces instant and absolute rejection. The mechanism is the scar tissue of the soul: accumulated negative volition toward the first advent has produced such hardness of heart that the initial hearing is the last genuine hearing. Each subsequent hearing is processed through increasing layers of scar tissue until the person no longer recognizes what is being rejected.

This is the same phenomenon described in Romans 9:15–18, where the hardness of Israel is compared to the hardness of Pharaoh's heart. Pharaoh's negative volition was genuine at the first hearing; subsequent hardenings were the judicial confirmation of a decision already made. The parallel with Israel's sustained negative volition toward the first advent is exact.

The Jews of the tribulation will still be looking for the Messiah to come — because for them there is no first advent. They accepted the rituals of the Mosaic Law without accepting the reality the rituals pointed to. They can perform the ceremonies, observe the feasts, read the prophets, and still say no — because they have said no so many times, and built scar tissue so thoroughly, that the ritual has been entirely separated from its content. Reformed Judaism is the institutionalization of this separation: the ritual maintained, the reality excluded.

When every eye sees him at the second advent — when the Omega glory of Christ is manifest universally — those who have blotted out the first advent will experience, in one lucid moment, the full recognition of what they have rejected. That is the content of kopto. That is the frustration Revelation 1:7 introduces. And that is the negative pole around which the entire positive subject of Romans 11 will be structured.

V. Introduction to Romans 11: Scope and Method

Romans 11 is the culmination of the three-chapter unit beginning at Romans 9. Romans 9 established the sovereignty of God in election and the hardening of unbelieving Israel. Romans 10 addressed the universality of the gospel and Israel's responsibility in rejecting it. Romans 11 will synthesize these themes and add what neither chapter addresses alone: the future of Israel in the plan of God, the theological significance of the Jewish remnant, and the implications of Israel's history for the Church Age believer.

The analytical method of Romans 11 is to use Israel as a controlled case study in the operation of divine justice. Israel possessed, in maximum degree, everything that makes spiritual advance possible: the covenants, the canon, the prophets, the Messiah himself. The response of Israel — both positive and negative — illustrates with precision what divine blessing and divine discipline look like when the protocol plan of God is operating at full scale against a clearly defined historical entity.

Because that same protocol plan operates in the soul of every individual believer — because the same categories of positive volition, doctrine intake, momentum, maturity, and divine blessing apply to the individual as to the nation — Israel's history is not merely Jewish history. It is the photograph of every soul that has ever been regenerate. Romans 11 will be studied with that double register throughout: what it says about Israel, and what it reveals about the believer.

Conclusions from Chapter Six Hundred Ninety

1. Revelation 1:7 establishes the time of the second advent and identifies two categories of Jews who will be present on the earth at that moment: Jewish believers and Jewish unbelievers. The unbelievers are those who are guilty of the big blot out in their generation.

2. The big blot out is maximum negative volition toward the first advent of Christ, sustained through repeated rejection until scar tissue of the soul produces a complete blackout of the first advent from Jewish consciousness. The pattern begins with a genuine hearing and genuine rejection; subsequent rejections are processed through increasing hardness of heart, confirming and deepening the original decision.

3. The lamentation of kopto at the second advent is frustration, not repentance. Jewish unbelievers who survived the tribulation with its maximum supernatural evangelism — by the 144,000, Moses and Elijah, and angelic messengers — and still said no will recognize at the second advent what they rejected. They will be removed from the earth by the baptism of fire. Their frustration at that moment represents the terminal expression of the big blot out.

4. The principle of kopto applies individually to every Church Age believer in the moment of physical death. Whatever was neglected — doctrine intake, momentum in the protocol plan, the use of the daily provisions of logistical grace — becomes vivid at the point of departure. The believer dying the sin unto death experiences a frustration analogous in kind to the lamentation of Revelation 1:7. The mature believer dying in dying grace carries into eternity the accumulated treasure of epignosis.

5. The heritage of the royal family of God exceeds even the heritage of Israel because it is eternal, unconditional, and permanent. Possessing such a heritage and neglecting it — in favor of the attractions and distractions of the details of life — is the individual believer's form of the big blot out.

6. Christ's self-identification as Alpha and Omega in Revelation 1:8 establishes two phases of his glory. Alpha designates his eternal divine essence — co-equal, co-eternal second person of the Trinity, creator of the universe, God of Israel. Omega designates the glory of the hypostatic union — initiated at the virgin birth, encompassing the cross, resurrection, ascension, and session, and to be permanently manifest at the second advent and throughout the millennium.

7. The Jewish race was founded on recognition of the first advent of Christ. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were regenerate through faith in Christ as Savior and God. The entire Mosaic sacrificial system was structured to present the first advent in detail. The big blot out is therefore not merely negative volition toward a religious proposition; it is the rejection of the very foundation of Jewish identity.

8. Israel's history in Romans 11 functions as a photograph of the individual believer's soul. The same protocol plan that governed Israel's corporate history governs the individual believer's spiritual life. The patterns of positive volition, doctrine intake, momentum, the maturity barrier, supergrace blessing, negative volition, scar tissue, reversionism, and divine discipline — all are present in Israel's history and all apply to the individual soul. Romans 11 will be studied with this double register throughout.

9. The mind was designed to operate on truth, not falsehood. Every rejection of truth opens the soul to falsehood. Sustained negative volition produces scar tissue of the soul, which in turn generates the vacuum of the soul — an attraction toward what is false. The phenomenon is universal: it operates in individuals, in client nations, and in the nation of Israel. Romans 11 will demonstrate from Israel's history how this principle operates at the national level, and what the justice of God does in response.

Glossary

hostis ὅστις hostis — qualitative relative pronoun A compound relative pronoun (hos + tis) that designates persons belonging to a specific category, not merely identifying them. In Revelation 1:7 it designates the category of Jewish unbelievers who pierced Christ — i.e., those guilty of the big blot out in every generation.
ekkenteo ἐκκεντέω ekkenteo — to pierce Compound verb: ek (out) + kenteo (to prick, pierce). In Revelation 1:7, the constative aorist gathers into one entirety every act of Jewish rejection of Christ that constitutes the big blot out. The piercing of Christ at the cross is the historical focal point; the verb encompasses all Jewish negative volition toward his first advent.
phyle φυλή phyle — tribe Noun denoting a tribe or clan grouping. In Revelation 1:7, the plural with the genitive of reference from ge (the land) specifies the tribes of Israel with reference to the holy land, correcting the broader rendering 'kindreds of the earth.'
ge γῆ ge — earth, land Noun with a semantic range from 'earth' (the planet or the world) to 'land' (a specific geographic territory). In Revelation 1:7 the genitive singular of reference specifies the holy land — the land of Israel — rather than the earth in general.
kopto κόπτω kopto — to strike, to lament Verb meaning to strike, cut, or beat. In the middle voice it denotes the striking of one's own breast as a gesture of mourning or lamentation. In Revelation 1:7 the future middle indicative describes the lamentation of Jewish unbelievers at the second advent — not repentance but frustration at irreversible loss.
alpha ἄλφα alpha — first letter of the Greek alphabet As a title of Christ in Revelation 1:8, Alpha designates his eternal divine essence — co-equal and co-eternal second person of the Trinity, creator of the universe, God of Israel. The Alpha glory of Christ antedates creation and is related to his divine essence and divine integrity.
omega ὦ omega — last letter of the Greek alphabet As a title of Christ in Revelation 1:8, Omega designates the glory of the hypostatic union, beginning with the virgin birth and encompassing the full scope of his incarnate work: impeccability, redemption, reconciliation, propitiation, resurrection, ascension, session, and the second advent. The Omega glory will be permanently manifest at the second advent and throughout the millennium.
big blot out Technical term for maximum Jewish negative volition toward the first advent of Christ. The blot out is not simple unbelief but sustained, repeated rejection that builds scar tissue of the soul until the first advent is entirely absent from Jewish consciousness. Jewish unbelievers will accept virtually any characterization of Jesus of Nazareth except the identification of him as the God of Israel and Savior of mankind. Described in Romans 9 by analogy with the hardening of Pharaoh's heart.
hypostatic union The union of full, undiminished deity and true, genuine humanity in the one person of Jesus Christ, without mixture, confusion, or subtraction of either nature. The hypostatic union began at the virgin birth and continues eternally. Christ's Omega glory is the glory of the hypostatic union manifest to mankind.
baptism of fire The judgment that removes all unbelievers — both Jewish and Gentile — from the earth at the conclusion of the tribulation, immediately before the inauguration of the millennium. Unbelievers surviving the tribulation are not permitted to enter the millennial kingdom. The baptism of fire is the instrument of their removal.
epignosis ἐπίγνωσις epignosis — full, exact knowledge The category of knowledge required for spiritual growth — not merely intellectual acquaintance with doctrine (gnosis) but the metabolized, fully perceived knowledge that has been transferred from the human spirit to the right lobe through the ministry of the Holy Spirit. Epignosis is the content that constitutes the believer's permanent spiritual treasure; it accompanies the soul beyond physical death.

Chapter Six Hundred Ninety-One

Revelation 1:7–8 — Alpha and Omega: Preparing for Romans 11

Revelation 1:7 “Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him, and all tribes of the earth will wail on account of him. Even so. Amen.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: Behold, He is coming with clouds, and every eye shall see Him, also those who pierced Him; and all of the tribes with reference to the land shall lament over Him. Yes, I believe it.
Revelation 1:8 “"I am the Alpha and the Omega," says the Lord God, "who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty."” (ESV)
Corrected translation: I am the Alpha and the Omega — eternal God and Christ in hypostatic union — says the Lord our God: He who is, first advent of Christ; both He who was, eternal God in Alpha glory; and He who is coming, second advent in Omega glory, the omnipotent ruler.

This chapter concludes a multi-session introduction to Romans chapter 11 by working through Revelation 1:7–8. The title Alpha and Omega — the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet — encodes the full arc of Christ's glory: His eternal existence as God of Israel (Alpha glory) and His incarnate, redemptive, and eschatological work from the virgin birth through the millennium (Omega glory). The concept of the 'big blot out' — maximum Jewish negative volition toward the first advent — provides the theological bridge between this passage in Revelation and what Paul will argue in Romans 11.

I. Revelation 1:7 — The Second Advent and the Big Blot Out

Revelation 1:7 describes the second advent of Christ as a moment of universal visibility: every eye will see Him, including those who pierced Him. The phrase 'those who pierced Him' carries covenantal weight. The tribes lamenting 'with reference to the land' are specifically Israel — the covenant nation whose unbelieving majority has, across successive generations, rejected the first advent of their own God.

This rejection is what the text calls the 'big blot out': a process by which maximum negative volition toward the gospel progressively erases from consciousness the very first advent that constitutes the center of Israel's spiritual heritage. Each successive refusal adds a layer of scar tissue to the soul — what the King James Version renders 'hardness of heart' — until the individual can no longer perceive the truth being presented and comes instead to believe the substitute lie. The lament at the second advent is thus the moment of recognition: they see the One they rejected and whose rejection they could not undo.

The dynamics of this process are not unique to Israel. The same mechanism — sustained negative volition producing scar tissue of the soul, which opens the soul's vacuum to receive and ultimately believe falsehood — operates wherever a people possessing spiritual heritage progressively rejects it. Scripture illustrates the pattern with Pharaoh in Romans 9:15–18: a hardened heart is not an arbitrary divine act but the judicial confirmation of repeated, self-chosen refusal.

II. Revelation 1:8 — Alpha and Omega as a Title of Christ

A. The Phrase 'Beginning and Ending' — A Textual Note

The phrase 'the beginning and the ending' found in the Textus Receptus and reflected in the King James Version is absent from the ancient manuscripts. It is a scribal addition and is not treated as canonical here.

B. The Verb Lego and Its Force

The verb rendered 'says' is the present active indicative of legō (λέγω). The present tense here is a perfective present: it denotes the continuation of existing results. The Omega glory of Christ — inaugurated at the first advent — is an already-established reality that persists into the present. The active voice indicates that Christ Himself produces this declaration. The indicative mood marks it as an unqualified statement of doctrine, not condition or wish.

C. Kurios Ho Theos — Lord Our God

With legō comes the nominative singular subject Kyrios (Κύριος), the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew tetragrammaton rendered as Adonai in synagogue reading. To this is added the appositional nominative ho Theos (ὁ Θεός), yielding the full construction Kyrios ho Theos. This is the precise Greek equivalent of the Hebrew Adonai Elohenu ('the LORD our God') from Deuteronomy 6:4. The two expressions are synonymous across three languages: Hebrew, Greek, and the English rendering 'the Lord our God.' Both refer to the Lord Jesus Christ as the God of Israel.

D. The Three Participial Phrases

The title Alpha and Omega is then explicated by three participial expressions that span the full range of Christ's existence and work.

1. He Who Is — First Advent and the Beginning of Omega Glory

The first expression is the articular present active participle of eimi (εἰμί), rendered 'he who is.' The present tense is a static present, emphasizing the perpetually existing reality of the hypostatic union: Christ is the God-man now, at the right hand of the Father. The definite article functions as a personal pronoun, identifying this expression with the Lord Jesus Christ as God of Israel and linking Kyrios ho Theos to Adonai Elohenu. This phrase points to the first advent — the virgin birth — as the beginning of Omega glory.

2. He Who Was — Alpha Glory and Eternal Existence

The second expression uses the imperfect active indicative of eimi (εἰμί). The imperfect here is a progressive imperfect of description: the eternal existence of Christ as God is represented as actually ongoing in past time, present time, and forever. There never was a moment when Christ did not exist. This is His Alpha glory — undiminished deity, co-equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, Creator of the universe (John 1:3; Colossians 1:16; Hebrews 1:10).

3. He Who Is Coming — Second Advent and the End of Omega Glory

The third expression is the articular present active participle of erchomai (ἔρχομαι), 'He who is coming.' The present tense here is futuristic: the event has not yet occurred but is so certain in the mind of the writer that it is presented as already in motion — equivalent to the Hebrew prophetic perfect. Erchomai is a deponent verb, middle or passive in form but active in meaning. This circumstantial participle denotes the second advent as the concluding expression of Omega glory, encompassing the millennial reign, the great white throne judgment, and the eternal state.

E. Pantokrator — The Omnipotent Ruler

The title concludes with Pantokratōr (Παντοκράτωρ), used in apposition via the generic definite article. It is a compound: panto (all) + kratōr (ruler), yielding 'the all-powerful ruler' or 'omnipotent one.' In this context it specifies the nature of Christ's authority at the second advent and confirms that erchomai refers to the second advent. When Christ returns, He comes as the omnipotent sovereign to rule the world during the millennium.

III. The Shema and the Alpha–Omega Title

The most elemental expression of Jewish worship is Deuteronomy 6:4, the Shema:

Shema Yisrael — 'Hear [concentrate], O Israel' — followed by Adonai Elohenu, 'the LORD our God,' and Adonai Echad (אֲדֹנָי אֶחָד), 'the LORD is one' or 'the LORD is unique.' The term echad (אֶחָד) carries both the sense of numerical oneness and of uniqueness. Applied to Jesus Christ as the God of Israel, it is theological precision: of the three members of the Godhead, only the Lord Jesus Christ is the God of Israel. He is unique further in that He is the God-man — undiminished deity and true humanity in one person forever (hypostatic union). The term Emanuel (עִמָּנוּ אֵל), 'God with us,' composed of the preposition im (with) and the noun El (God), names precisely this event: the first advent, the beginning of Omega glory.

The Shema thus encodes both Alpha glory (Jehovah is our God — the eternal God of Israel) and Omega glory (the LORD is unique — the God-man in hypostatic union). The two are inseparable. In the big blot out, Israel accepts Alpha glory — they affirm that Jesus Christ is the eternal God of Israel — but they blot out the Omega glory, the first advent. Yet they continue to recite the Shema in every generation. The ritual persists; the reality has been evacuated. Ritual without reality is meaningless, and this is the tragedy the Shema itself diagnoses when read against Revelation 1:8.

IV. Alpha Glory and Omega Glory Distinguished

Alpha glory designates the eternal existence and attributes of Jesus Christ as God prior to and apart from the incarnation. As Alpha God He is the Creator of the universe (John 1:3; Colossians 1:16; Hebrews 1:10), the beginning of history for humanity in general and for Israel specifically. He is co-equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, possessing the full complement of divine attributes — omniscience, omnipotence, omnipresence, sovereignty, righteousness, justice, love, eternal life, and immutability. In Alpha glory, the omniscience of Christ foreknew every thought, every decision, and every action of every person in all of history, and this information was the content of the divine decrees.

Omega glory designates everything that pertains to Jesus Christ as the God-man in hypostatic union. It begins at the virgin birth — the incarnation — and encompasses His impeccable life, substitutionary work on the cross, bodily resurrection, ascension, and present session at the right hand of the Father. Omega glory extends forward to the second advent, the millennial reign, and the eternal state. Omega glory is not possessed by the Father or the Spirit; it belongs to the Son uniquely as the God-man. This is the glory that unbelieving Israel has blotted out and that they will confront at the second advent.

The Father and the Spirit share Alpha glory with the Son. Only the Son has Omega glory. It is precisely this uniqueness — His true humanity, Jewish in the line of David, resurrected and seated at the Father's right hand in that humanity — that constitutes the historical stumbling block to Israel and the irreducible content of the gospel.

V. The Covenantal Significance of Alpha and Omega for Israel

The Jewish race was founded on recognition of the God of Israel as both Alpha and Omega. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are distinguished from their respective relatives — Chaldean, Edomite, Ishmaelite — not by ethnicity alone but by faith in the Lord Jesus Christ as both their God and their Savior. They believed and advanced to spiritual maturity. This is what qualifies the Abrahamic line as the line of Israel in the theological sense, not merely the biological one. As Paul will argue in Romans 9, not all who are of Israel by descent are truly Israel in the spiritual sense.

The Alpha and Omega title is therefore the last great evangelistic approach to Israel in the Tribulation. The 144,000 Jewish evangelists, the resurrected witnesses, the angelic proclamation immediately before the second advent — all present the gospel to a generation of Jews who have, by accumulated negative volition, blotted out the Omega glory of their own God. The title Alpha and Omega in Revelation 1:8 recapitulates Deuteronomy 6:4, bringing that original covenant statement to its eschatological fulfillment.

The Davidic covenant promised an eternal son who would reign forever. Jesus Christ in Omega glory fulfills this covenant. Regenerate Israel — those who have believed in Christ through any generation of Jewish history — will enter the millennial kingdom as a restored client nation. The unregenerate, those who have sustained the big blot out to the end, will face the baptism of fire, the judgment that removes them from entry into the kingdom.

VI. Historical Pattern: The Big Blot Out and National Judgment

The big blot out is not a uniquely Jewish phenomenon in its mechanism, even though its specific content — rejection of the first advent of the God of Israel — is unique to the Jewish people. The same causal sequence operates wherever a people possessing spiritual heritage progressively rejects it: negative volition produces scar tissue of the soul, which opens the soul's vacuum to receive falsehood, which is then believed as reality. This is the explanation for the cyclical collapse of nations that possessed spiritual heritage — Assyria, Babylon, Persia, and eventually Rome — each of which experienced catastrophic historical judgment when accumulated negative volition reached critical mass.

For Israel specifically, the periodic Holocaust — most visibly the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 CE and the events of the Nazi era — functions as a historical judgment corresponding to accumulated rejection of the Omega glory of Christ. This is not arbitrary divine punishment but the judicial outworking of the five cycles of discipline, the pattern Moses delineated in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. Anti-Semitism is historically conspicuous precisely because Israel's covenant relationship with God makes the spiritual causation visible; the same mechanism operates, less visibly, in Gentile nations as well.

Moses in Deuteronomy 10–14 first prophesied the big blot out — a point Paul has already argued in Romans chapter 10. Isaiah's lament, 'Lord, who has believed our report?' (Isaiah 53:1, cited in Romans 10:16), expresses the same recognition: the full witness to the first advent was given; the majority rejected it. The prophet speaks from within the accumulated weight of that rejection.

VII. The Deuteronomy 6 Shema as a Positive Model for Doctrine in the Soul

Deuteronomy 6:4–7 does not merely describe ritual; it describes the positive alternative to the big blot out. Verse 5 commands Israel to love the LORD their God with all of the right lobe — the faculty of rational thought and doctrinal comprehension — with all of the soul, and with all concentration. This command presupposes that truth must be resident in the right lobe before love of any category becomes possible. Capacity for love — whether personal or impersonal — is a function of truth in the soul, not of emotion. Emotion is a responder to the right lobe, not its director. When emotion governs rather than responds, the result is sentimentality, instability, and ultimately the vacuum that draws in the lie.

Verse 6 commands that these doctrines be in the right lobe — not merely memorized as words but comprehended, categorized, and available for application. This is the daily function of the grace apparatus for perception (GAP): the consistent intake of Bible doctrine through the ministry of God the Holy Spirit, moving truth from academic knowledge into the category of epignosis — full, exact, operational knowledge — resident in the right lobe of the soul.

Verse 7 extends the principle intergenerationally: you shall teach these doctrines diligently to your children. The covenant community is responsible for creating the conditions under which the next generation encounters truth before the vacuum of the soul can be filled with falsehood. The alternative is a generation trained to believe a lie — one that will eventually act out the consequences of that training in every domain of life.

Conclusions from Chapter Six Hundred Ninety-One

1. Jesus Christ as Alpha God has no beginning. He is the Creator of the universe (John 1:3; Colossians 1:16; Hebrews 1:10), the beginning of history for humanity in general and for Israel specifically. There never was a time when He did not exist.

2. As Alpha God, the omniscience of Christ foreknew all of history. Every thought, every decision, and every action of every person who has ever lived was known to Him before the creation of humanity. This foreknowledge is the content of the divine decrees.

3. Jesus Christ in Omega glory is the end of human history. His Omega glory encompasses the second advent, the millennial reign, the great white throne judgment, and the eternal state. He is the Alpha and the Omega — beginning and end.

4. Omega glory begins at the first advent. The virgin birth is the beginning of Omega glory. The title Emanuel — God with us — names this inaugurating event. Omega glory cannot exist without the incarnation.

5. Alpha glory and Omega glory belong inseparably to the same person. The Shema — Adonai Elohenu, Adonai Echad — encodes both in its two lines. The first line affirms Alpha glory; the second points to Omega glory in the uniqueness of the God-man. To reject Omega glory while affirming Alpha glory is to fracture what God has joined.

6. The big blot out is the progressive erasure of the first advent from Jewish consciousness. It is produced by repeated negative volition toward the gospel, each refusal adding scar tissue to the soul, opening the soul's vacuum to receive and ultimately believe the lie. The ritual of the Shema continues; the reality the Shema encodes has been suppressed.

7. The Father and the Spirit share Alpha glory; only the Son has Omega glory. His true humanity — Jewish in the line of David, bodily resurrected, and perpetually existing as the God-man — is the unique dimension of His glory that no other member of the Godhead possesses.

8. The Davidic covenant is fulfilled in Omega glory. Jesus Christ returns at the second advent as Son of David and Son of God. He comes to fulfill unconditionally what was promised to David: an eternal son, an eternal throne, an eternal kingdom. Regenerate Israel enters that kingdom; unregenerate Israel faces the baptism of fire.

9. Kyrios ho Theos and Adonai Elohenu are precisely synonymous. Revelation 1:8 takes the Hebrew formula of Deuteronomy 6:4 and renders it in Greek for the eschatological context of the Tribulation. The same Jesus Christ who is the God of Israel in Deuteronomy is the Alpha and the Omega in Revelation — identified by the same title across both Testaments.

10. Pantokrator — the omnipotent ruler — defines the character of the second advent. When Christ returns He comes not as a suffering servant but as the all-powerful sovereign to establish and govern the millennial kingdom. This title confirms that the third participial phrase in Revelation 1:8 refers specifically to the second advent.

Term Greek / Transliteration Definition
Alpha glory Alpha glory The eternal divine glory of Jesus Christ as God prior to and apart from the incarnation. Encompasses His eternal existence, His role as Creator, and the full complement of divine attributes. Shared in essence by all three members of the Godhead.
Omega glory Omega glory The glory of Jesus Christ as the God-man in hypostatic union. Begins at the virgin birth (first advent) and extends through the cross, resurrection, ascension, session, second advent, millennial reign, and eternal state. Unique to the Son; not possessed by the Father or the Spirit.
